name: @shepherd/ext-diagnostics
description: shepherd.diagnostics — the built-in you invoke to find out whether the extension host is alive.
//exports: Two subpaths on purpose: main imports ./manifest to register the extension, and only the utility process imports the root (which pulls in `activate`). One entry would drag the extension's code into the main bundle to read six fields of metadata.
//shepherd: The manifest, as an extension declares it. `src/manifest.ts` is the typed copy the host actually loads, and `manifest.test.ts` asserts the two are identical — a built-in is held to the same validation as anybody else, so it must not be able to drift from its own package.json.
//ui: The UI half, imported ONLY by the renderer (boundaries.js). It is a separate subpath because it is a separate PROCESS: `.` is the service half and runs in a utility process with no DOM, and react must not follow it there.
